subtopics.title: Two Sectors, One Set of Concepts

questions.question: The key difference between the formal and informal sectors, according to the lesson, is:
options: The formal sector understands profit; the informal sector does not
The concepts differ completely between the sectors
The concepts are identical; what differs is the recording of them
The informal sector has no capital

questions.question: A spaza shop's fridge is classified as:
options: Stock, because it can be sold
A fixed asset — a possession kept for use, not resale

questions.question: Profit, in both sectors, is defined as:
options: Cash in the tin at month end

questions.question: The supermarket's R500 000 bank deposit and the spaza owner's R3 000 saved cash are BOTH examples of:
options: Capital — the owner's resources committed to the business

questions.question: A cooldrink bought for R8 and sold for R12 illustrates:
options: Cost price R8, selling price R12 — a margin of R4
Cost price R12, selling price R8
Income of R8 and an expense of R12

questions.question: Why does the spaza owner's profit often look better than it truly is?
options: Her stock is cheaper than the supermarket's
Her own unpaid labour is an invisible cost that never reduces the profit figure
Informal profits are always overstated by law

subtopics.title: Where the Difference Bites — Records and Decisions

questions.question: A profitable informal trader is refused a bank loan. The most likely accounting reason is:
options: Informal traders may not open bank accounts
Without records she cannot PROVE her income — unrecorded success is invisible

questions.question: Taking school fees from the shop's cash tin and 'restocking later' violates which principle?
options: The business entity rule — business and owner's money must be kept apart
No principle — the money belongs to the owner anyway

questions.question: The lesson's verdict on informal traders is that:
options: They are poor businesspeople rescued by formal accounting
Business skill exists; recording ADDS proof, accuracy, separation and continuity to it
They should avoid records to stay flexible
Their methods have nothing in common with formal accounting

questions.question: In a stokvel, the treasurer's book of who paid and whose turn is next corresponds to which modern record?
options: A ledger of contributions and claims

questions.question: Cattle held as countable, visible wealth correspond most closely to:
options: Recorded fixed assets — a store of capital the owner can verify

questions.question: Communal grazing rules, with elders checking that nobody overgrazes, demonstrate:
options: Internal control — agreed rules over resource use, with someone trusted to monitor

questions.question: The R3 000 the spaza owner saved to start her shop is her:
The bread and airtime she buys at the wholesaler to sell again are her:
Her taxi fare to the wholesaler and the fridge's electricity are:
options: Expenses — money spent to keep the shop running

questions.question: Head-count: R4 500 in, R3 000 stock — 'about R1 500 profit'. The notebook adds taxi R160, electricity R90, airtime R50. True profit is:
The R300 gap between the head's answer and the notebook's answer exists because:
options: The notebook made an arithmetic error
Small expenses leak from memory, quietly inflating the profit figure
Profit is always R300 lower on paper

questions.question: Why should the owner's own unpaid work eventually appear in her figures?
options: Because SARS demands it for spaza shops
It should not — unpaid work is free
Labour is a real cost; counting it lets her compare the shop honestly against earning a wage elsewhere

questions.question: In stokvel terms, the rule that a member who skips two months cannot claim a payout is:
The December meeting where the treasurer accounts for every rand is the stokvel's version of:
The lesson's closing takeaway is that formal accounting:
options: Replaces community practices that never worked
Formalises familiar practices — sharper tools for instincts communities already trust
Is unrelated to anything before textbooks
